chunks: And ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī ʿAbdillāh narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about a man who owed a kurr of food, then purchased a kurr from another man, and he said to the man: 'Go and take your due in full.' He said: 'There is no harm in that.'

key_terms.فَاسْتَوْفِ: take in full or collect completely
key_terms.فَاشْتَرَى: he purchased in a sale transaction
key_terms.كُرٌّ: a fixed measure or quantity of food
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: there is no harm in it; it is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible in Islamic law to direct a seller to take his measure from food already owed by the buyer?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding a debt in food and a subsequent purchase involving the same measure. The Imam عليه السلام states that there is no harm in directing the seller to collect his due from the food already owed, indicating the permissibility of such an arrangement in transaction law.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3773 - Abd Al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah narrated from Abu Abdillah (as):

I asked him about a man who owed a kurr (a measure) of food and then purchased a kurr from another man. He said to the seller, "Go and take your right (measure) from the food I owe."
Imam (as) said: "There is no harm in that."
